subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable core TUI plain-text accessibility setting, and what public config key, default, and ASCII replacement semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the setting name, default, and replacement text become a public config contract and affect all TUI users.

options.title: Add Bounded TUI Plain-Text Mode
options.body: Implement an opt-in core TUI setting with ASCII replacements across tool cards, selectors, config metadata, docs, and tests while keeping rich glyph output as the default.

options.title: Pause Until Semantics Are Chosen
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer implementation until maintainers choose the key, default, and replacement strings.

options.title: Reject Core Config For Now
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide glyph suppression should not be a core TUI capability despite the screen-reader reports.

recommendation.title: Add Bounded TUI Plain-Text Mode
recommendation.body: Implement an opt-in core TUI setting with ASCII replacements across tool cards, selectors, config metadata, docs, and tests while keeping rich glyph output as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is original and recent ownership across TUI, tool-display, and config surfaces.
